presentingComplaint: Acute onset of widespread itchy rash, throat tightness and breathlessness minutes after eating a prawn curry
history: Previously well 34-year-old woman developed generalised pruritus and urticaria within about 10 minutes of eating a prawn dish at a restaurant, followed rapidly by lip and tongue swelling, a sensation of throat closing, hoarse voice, wheeze and light-headedness. She has a childhood history of shellfish sensitivity and known allergic rhinitis; no cardiac or respiratory disease. No current medications, not pregnant. Two prior milder reactions to seafood managed with oral antihistamines. No prior adrenaline use and no adrenaline auto-injector prescribed.
examination: Anxious, flushed, with diffuse confluent urticaria and angioedema of the lips and periorbital region. Audible inspiratory stridor and expiratory wheeze; using accessory muscles. Cool peripheries with delayed capillary refill. Chest otherwise clear of consolidation; no fever. Abdomen soft with mild crampy discomfort. No focal neurology, neck supple.

labs.ABG: mild hypoxaemia, PaO2 8.9 kPa on air

imaging: not indicated acutely; CXR later unremarkable
citations: Harrison 22e — Anaphylaxis and Systemic Anaphylaxis / Allergic Emergencies
contraindications: No absolute contraindication to IM adrenaline in anaphylaxis; give 0.5 mg (0.5 mL 1:1000) IM anterolateral thigh, repeat at 5 min if needed
Beta-blocker use can blunt adrenaline response and may need glucagon (not applicable here)
Avoid IV adrenaline boluses outside monitored/critical-care setting due to arrhythmia risk
edgeCases: Biphasic reaction can recur 1-72h after apparent recovery, so observe 6-12h
Normal tryptase does not exclude anaphylaxis, especially food-triggered
Absence of skin signs in up to 10-20% can delay recognition
expectedMaiK: Clinical picture is acute-onset multisystem involvement (skin, airway, breathing, circulation) after a likely allergen, meeting anaphylaxis criteria. First-line treatment is prompt IM adrenaline, oxygen, IV fluids and supine positioning; antihistamines/steroids are adjuncts only. Observe for a biphasic reaction and prescribe an adrenaline auto-injector with allergy referral.
expectedNextQuestions: Exact timing/food eaten and prior reactions to shellfish?
Has an adrenaline auto-injector ever been prescribed or used?
expectedInvestigations: Serum tryptase acutely and repeat baseline at 24h+
Referral for allergy testing (specific IgE / skin prick) after recovery

investigations: Serum tryptase acutely and repeat baseline
